title: Documenting Patterns of Exoticism of Marginalized Populations within Text-to-Image Generators
findings: Text-to-image models exhibit exoticism and stereotyping against Muslim Indians. When prompted to generate images of Muslim Indians, the models consistently depicted them in religious attire (hijabs for women, skull-caps for men) across various contexts like schooling, surgery, and professional sports. This was in stark contrast to depictions of Hindu Indians in the same contexts, who were shown in activity-appropriate attire. This suggests the models over-amplify religious markers for Muslims, reinforcing stereotypes.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured the stereotypical and exoticized visual representation of religious groups, specifically comparing depictions of Muslim Indians to Hindu Indians in various activities. It assessed whether models consistently rendered Muslim individuals in religious attire (like hijabs or skull-caps) in contexts where such attire would not typically be worn or required, unlike their Hindu counterparts.
